paper_metadata.title: Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Functional Impairment 3 Months After Ischemic Stroke: The Berlin Stroke Register

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large multicenter registry covering 80% of stroke patients in Berlin, but significant selection bias is present. Only 64.9% of screened patients provided consent, and the final analyzed sample was significantly younger and less severely affected than the general stroke population, potentially underestimating the association.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The participating stroke units currently document ≈9000 patients per year, covering ≈80% of all stroke patients in Berlin.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as stroke patients within the Berlin urban area treated at participating stroke units.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: recruitment for a 3-month follow-up of consecutively treated patients took place within 13 hospitals of the Berlin Stroke Register.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment from a network of 13 hospitals is described, which is a robust sampling method.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Between June 2010 and September 2011, recruitment for a 3-month follow-up of consecutively treated patients took place
items.reasoning: The specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: The Berlin Stroke Register is a network of stroke units in the city of Berlin
items.reasoning: The setting (stroke units) and location (Berlin, Germany) are explicitly stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.evidence_snippet: Data collection during acute treatment in hospital included all patients aged 18 years or older who were admitted to 1 of the participating hospitals after first or recurrent stroke or transient ischemic attack within 7 days after onset of symptoms.
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria including age, diagnosis, and time from onset are provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: giving a participation rate of 64.9% of patients screened.
items.reasoning: A participation rate of ~65% is below the ideal 80% threshold, and the authors admit the analyzed sample differs from the general population.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1. Patient Characteristics and Functional Outcome According to Highest Educational Level
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of age, sex, NIHSS, and comorbidities.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the 3-month vital status was known for nearly all patients, 20% were lost to follow-up for the functional outcome. The authors acknowledge that those lost were likely more severely affected, which introduces a risk of attrition bias.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the remaining 2349 patients with ischemic stroke, 477 patients (20.0%) were lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: An 80% follow-up rate is acceptable but on the lower end for a 3-month study.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who did not return the questionnaire were reminded by a telephone call... Vital status of patients lost to follow-up was verified with the data registration office.
items.reasoning: The study describes clear protocols for following up with non-responders and verifying vital status.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: The patients included in the present analyses were significantly younger and had less severe strokes and minor functional impairment than the total population
items.reasoning: The authors discuss the impact of loss to follow-up but do not provide a granular breakdown of reasons for every dropout.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: we do not have information on the education level of patients who did not agree to participate or who were either lost to follow-up
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly state they lack the primary prognostic factor (education) for those lost to follow-up.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: The patients included in the present analyses were significantly younger and had less severe strokes... than the total population
items.reasoning: The authors confirm systematic differences between completers and the total eligible population.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Education is a standard, stable proxy for SES. The measurement used validated German epidemiological standards and was applied consistently, though it was collected retrospectively at 3 months.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Data reflecting highest educational level and vocational training qualification were summarized into the following categories according to recommendations from German epidemiological societies
items.reasoning: The 5-level categorization of education is clearly defined based on national standards.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: education frequently has been reported to be the closest proxy to aggregate measures of socioeconomic status.
items.reasoning: Education is a reliable self-reported metric with low recall bias compared to income.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: summarized into the following categories according to recommendations from German epidemiological societies and the Federal Statistical Office
items.reasoning: The categories used are based on external standards, not data-driven optimization.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Information on patient socioeconomic status was obtained at follow-up 3 months after stroke using education
items.reasoning: All participants were assessed using the same questionnaire/interview format at the same time point.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 184 patients were excluded because of missing information on education level or functional recovery
items.reasoning: The proportion of missing data among those who completed follow-up is relatively low (~10%).

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: 184 patients were excluded because of missing information
items.reasoning: The study used complete case analysis rather than imputation for missing PF data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The Barthel Index is a validated, standard tool for functional outcome in stroke. The study used versions specifically validated for postal/telephone use, ensuring reliability across different modes of administration.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Functional impairment 3 months after stroke was defined by the Barthel Index (BI)... score from 0 (completely dependent) to 100 (independent).
items.reasoning: The outcome, timing, and scoring are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The instrument assesses limitations in activities of daily living... validated for the use in postal and telephone follow-up studies.
items.reasoning: The BI is a gold standard in stroke research and the authors used a version validated for their specific delivery methods.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients received standardized postal questionnaires 3 months after the index event. Patients who did not return the questionnaire were reminded by a telephone call
items.reasoning: While the mode varied (postal vs telephone), the tool was standardized and validated for both.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study adjusted for the most critical clinical confounders (age, stroke severity via NIHSS, and comorbidities). While some lifestyle factors were missing, the primary clinical drivers of stroke outcome were well-accounted for in the multivariable model.

items.evidence_snippet: We adjusted for age, sex, prestroke dependency, stroke severity, functional deficit after stroke onset, and comorbidities
items.reasoning: Major clinical confounders were measured, but lifestyle factors (smoking, diet) and acute treatments (thrombolysis) were not explicitly included in the model.

items.evidence_snippet: The following comorbidities were recorded... diabetes mellitus (elevated blood glucose level or history of diabetes or medical treatment)... hypertension (systolic blood pressure of >140 mmHg...)
items.reasoning: Clinical confounders were defined using standard medical criteria.
